title: Circuit Loop and the Missing Ground
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Open either wire of a simple sensor circuit and watch the charge stop moving. The missing-ground fault, made visible before you meet it on a real bench.

educational.topic: Circuit Loop and the Missing Ground
learningObjectives: Explain why a circuit must form a complete loop.
Predict what a sensor does when its ground wire is disconnected while power remains connected.
prerequisites: Knowing that electricity needs somewhere to go
Chapter 3 sections on voltage and current

keyQuestions: If the red wire is still connected, why is the sensor dead?
Does it matter which side of the loop you break?
What would a loose ground look like from across the room?
commonMisconceptions: Thinking of ground as an optional return, or as "just the negative side".
Believing a sensor with power connected must be at least partly working.
Blaming an intermittent reading on a faulty sensor rather than a faulty connection.
assessmentOpportunities: States that current requires a complete loop and names both wires as equally necessary.
Predicts that a sensor with power but no ground reads nothing at all.
Recognises intermittent readings as the signature of a loose connection rather than a broken sensor.
